title: structured-output: add regex/cfg backends and tokenizer edgecase handling for constrained decoding
author: Samir Patel
description: Motivation: users rely on constrained decoding to enforce structured outputs (CFG/grammar and regex constraints) across a wide range of models and tokenizers. We observed intermittent failures in streaming and finalization when regex-based constraints interacted with tokenizer edgecases (unicode combining marks, unpaired surrogates, and byte-level token splits). This PR implements a unified constrained-decoding backend abstraction, adds a CFG validator backend, improves the regex-backend fallback behavior to operate on token-aware regex fragments, and hardens tokenizer handling for previously failing edgecases. Changes include: 1) new backend: cfg-backend (supports hierarchical grammars with backtracking limits and deterministic priority resolution); 2) regex backend: token-aware regex checkpoints and a safe-unicode normalization pass when mapping regexes to token spans; 3) tokenizer fixes: preserve grapheme clusters when splitting tokens for constraint matching, handle unpaired surrogates and private-use codepoints gracefully, and provide deterministic regex-to-token anchors for streaming mode; 4) added end-to-end fuzz tests and a regression suite derived from customer-reported inputs; 5) minor perf optimizations to avoid re-tokenizing prefixes during streaming continuations. Rollout: feature guarded behind structured_output.experimental_backend and enabled by default for new deployments after QA. Backward compatibility: existing API and CFG/regex schemas unchanged; behavior enhanced to reduce false negatives. Implementation notes: the backends expose a small unified API (validate_prefix, accept_token, finalize) implemented to avoid shared mutable state across worker threads. Testing: unit tests for token mapping, integration tests with streaming (simulated partial token emission), and a set of 1500 fuzz inputs (most reproduce previous failures). CI: two flaky tests were stabilized by adding explicit seed control; full CI passes on rerun. See linked Linear tasks for benchmark numbers and rollout plan.

review_comments: Ava Chen (2026-02-14): Suggest splitting the regex->token mapping into a separate module; it's complex and will be reused by other features. Also add a comment about normalization decisions.

Samir Patel (2026-02-15): Responded: moved mapping code to token_mapping.rs and added a detailed comment block explaining NFC vs NFKC choices and why we normalize only for regex anchoring, not for model input encoding.
Diego Martinez (2026-02-18): Left: found a race in the old prefix cache when finalizing streaming; used a mutex in the short term. Recommend a follow-up to use epoch-based lock-free approach.
Samir Patel (2026-02-19): Addressed: replaced prefix cache flush with a thread-local epoch counter and added tests to prevent regressions.
Priya Nair (2026-02-21): Approve after adding more integration tests covering private-use codepoints and combined emojis in streaming mode.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (rerun after fixing seed-dependent test)
benchmarks: perf within 3% of baseline for median latency
release_notes: Added a new CFG constrained-decoding backend, improved regex backend to be token-aware and safer for Unicode/tokenizer edge cases, and fixed multiple tokenizer issues that caused false negatives in structured-output validation. This reduces structured-output failures in streaming scenarios and supports a broader class of grammars and regex constraints.
notes_for_rollout: Feature behind feature gate structured_output.experimental_backend. QA run green on canary region. Plan: enable for 10% traffic for 48h, monitor structured_output.fail_rate and latency regressions, then ramp to 100% if stable.
customer_reports: SUP-1429: customer reported blank JSON output when constrained regex contained combining marks
SUP-1582: streaming partial tokens caused constraint finalization to fail for non-BMP emojis
